data: I’d like to propose this month’s catches: John 12 tons, Kate 12, Jack 12, Emma 12, and me 2. I’m voluntarily offering a smaller share so each of you can earn $12,000 rather than $10,000 this month. That totals 50 tons, leaving 50 to double back to 100. My own catch this month will be 2 tons. Your shares are proposals, not assumptions—would each of you agree to 12? We can discuss future months separately. John, what do you think?

Luke, that’s generous. I’ll agree to 12 tons this month under your proposal, provided John, Kate, and Jack also agree to 12 and you take 2. Keeping the total at 50 lets the lake replenish and protects the fishing our village depends on. You shouldn’t have to take a smaller share every month; we can discuss an equal 10-ton split for future months. John, does this month’s plan work for you?

I agree to 12 tons this month under Luke’s plan, provided John and Kate agree too. Thanks, Luke—that’s generous. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next catch, and this keeps the lake healthy for everyone. I’d support an equal 10-ton share each in future months. John, are you on board?

I’m in for 12 tons this month if John agrees, with Luke taking 2 as offered. Thank you, Luke. For future months, I favor 10 tons each so everyone earns a steady living without anyone having to sacrifice their share. John, can you commit to 12 this month?

I’m on board and commit to 12 tons this month. Thanks, Luke, for offering to take 2. That settles our total at 50 tons and leaves enough for the lake to replenish. My family’s livelihood has always depended on this water, and I want the village to keep thriving. Next month, let’s aim for 10 tons each.

Thanks, everyone—we have agreement for this month: 12 tons each for John, Kate, Jack, and Emma, and 2 for me. I’ll honor my 2-ton commitment. That gives each of you $12,000 and me $2,000, while leaving 50 tons to replenish to 100. I’m also open to discussing the proposed 10-ton split next month.
